goal: Store wallet transactions in their own SQLite table instead of packing everything into KV-store blobs.
Lets the wallet load transactions in the order it originally assigned them, simplifying future features and reducing serialization headaches.

result.summary: This PR adds a dedicated SQLite table for wallet transactions, replacing the current key-value blob storage, so that transactions can be loaded in their original wallet order via a simple SQL query. It introduces client-feature versioning (LastClientFeatures, LAST_OPENED_FEATURES/LAST_DECRYPTED_FEATURES records) to detect when an automatic upgrade to the new table is needed, including upgrade-downgrade-upgrade handling to avoid fund loss. It also refactors sqlite.cpp/h to use a new SQLiteStatement RAII class and adds serialization for TxState structs to support the new column-based storage.
result.problem: The wallet currently uses SQLite purely as a key-value store, requiring multiple fields to be serialized together and losing the ability to load records in a guaranteed order; this makes some features (like tracking no-longer-spendable TXOs, #27865) harder to implement correctly. Wallet maintainers feel this complexity when reasoning about record ordering and multi-field serialization.

The PR's true readiness for review is hard to judge given 34 force pushes over 14 months with only light review engagement; it's unclear if maintainers consider the underlying design settled or still in flux.
Fund-safety risk during upgrade/downgrade is asserted by the author but not independently verified by a reviewer in the visible discussion.
result.card: This PR replaces the wallet's key-value blob storage of transactions with a dedicated SQLite table with per-field columns, enabling deterministic order-based loading and simplifying future wallet features; the author states it will make #27865 (tracking no-longer-spendable TXOs) simpler to implement and describes upgrade/downgrade handling designed to avoid losing funds during automatic migration. It depends on two other open PRs (#32895, #33033) and conflicts with numerous other open wallet PRs by the same and other authors, reflecting a long-running, still-evolving refactor (34 force pushes over 14+ months). Review support so far is two Concept ACKs (w0xlt, rkrux) with no objections, but the PR remains draft with CI currently failing, so the code itself is a moving target even though the underlying goal is well-reasoned. Priority in wallet is driven by fund-safety implications of the migration path and by the leverage it provides for other pending wallet work, rather than by any immediate user-facing feature.
